text: I’ll first inspect the STEP header and import it with OCCT/build123d to establish the declared units, assembly contents, solid count, validity, and overall scale before choosing a fluid-volume extraction method.

The import is a valid three-solid compound with dimensions consistent with millimetres, but the unit declaration was not in the header slice. I’ll locate the actual STEP unit entities, list each solid’s size/volume, and render the imported assembly to understand its topology before modifying it.

The file explicitly declares metres, but its numerical extents are only 0–54 if read literally; because STEP import reports 53.95 units and the object is a small blower-like assembly, I need to resolve whether OCCT has already converted a metre-authored model into millimetres. I’ll inspect the STEP contexts and render the three solids separately and in cutaway, which will also reveal the actual inlet/outlet openings and whether subtracting the material from a capped enclosure is appropriate.

The three bodies are stacked enclosure components rather than three fluid regions. Their STEP metre declaration is authoritative; OCCT/build123d appears to expose STEP coordinates in millimetre-like working units (a known CAD-kernel convention), so I will scale exported CFD geometry by 0.001 exactly once. Next I’ll quantify body overlaps and inventory planar/cylindrical faces; this determines whether the enclosed void can be extracted by boolean subtraction and identifies opening faces by topology rather than bounding-box guesses.
The first overlap probe encountered a null intersection (meaning at least one pair only touches), so I’ll repeat it with explicit null handling and continue the face inventory.

The face/volume inventory shows a critical CAD fact: these are three nearly solid enclosure pieces, not three fluid solids. I’ll inspect product names and exact section occupancy on several planes to determine whether a genuine enclosed cavity exists between the assembled bodies or whether the supplied assembly lacks an internal flow passage. I will not invent one if it is absent.

The imported CAD does not contain an internal flow volume to extract. OCCT reports exactly three valid solids and three shells—one exterior shell per solid, with no inner cavity shells. Section classification confirms the BODY and EMITTER interiors are fully occupied material across their cross-sections; all faces bound closed solids, so there are no inlet or outlet openings to cap or name. Creating a passage would require redesigning the supplied assembly, which the request forbids. I therefore cannot build a correct fluid mesh from this file.
